hot.pointer_line: On now: the new olive oil market at Glòries and the Women's Run this weekend, the Sagrada Família Christmas fair from 21 November, the lights on 26 November, the general election on 29 November, the MICHELIN Spain 2027 stars moved to 1 December, Mozart at the Liceu and the jazz festival's last weeks to 23 December.

groups.title: This weekend, 20–22 November
groups.desc: New oil at Glòries, a market reborn in Gràcia, and a Sunday of road closures.

items.name: The new olive oil and honey market, Glòries
items.teaser: This year's first-pressed oil from all five Catalan appellations, tasted at the stall, 20–22 November
items.story: November is when the new oil arrives: green, peppery and cloudy, pressed weeks ago. For its second edition the Mercat de l'Oli Nou i la Mel, run by the Catalan food agency Prodeca, brings nearly 50 extra-virgin producers from all five Catalan olive-oil appellations and 15 honey makers to Plaça de Josep Antoni Coderch at Glòries. There are cooking demonstrations, a showcase by the starred chef Fran López, and glasses of vi novell, the year's young wine.
items.why: Buy a litre of new arbequina for the galley: it is at its most pungent now and softens by spring.
facts: Plaça de Josep Antoni Coderch, Glòries
Free entry; oil and honey priced by the stall
Taste the oils side by side before you buy; the appellations differ more than you expect

items.name: Gràcia gets its market back: the new Abaceria
items.teaser: Rebuilt for €38m, the Mercat de l'Abaceria is back on its old site; the traders celebrate on Saturday 21
items.story: For years Gràcia shopped in a temporary market on Passeig de Sant Joan while its own was rebuilt. The new Mercat de l'Abaceria, a €38 million project with a ceramic, solar-panelled roof, opened on its original site from 17 November, with 30 stalls inside and 6 outside. On Saturday 21 November the traders throw an opening morning: a castellers workshop from 11:00 and a swing band from noon. Two spaces keep the late artist Amaia Arrazola's mural for the building site.
items.why: Go Saturday morning for the party, or any weekday before ten, when the fish is laid out and the regulars shop.
facts: Open from 17 Nov 2026; opening party Sat 21 Nov, 10:30–14:30
The temporary market on Passeig de Sant Joan closed on 14 November: do not go there

items.name: Sunday 22 November: the Women's Run, Barça, and a glass maze's last day
items.teaser: Road closures from 05:00, Barça v Villarreal at 14:00, the last day of the Mies pavilion's glass maze
items.story: Sunday starts early: the 22nd Cursa de les Dones sets off at 09:00 from Bac de Roda, crosses Clot, Poblenou and the Eixample, and finishes on Passeig de Pujades, with closures from 05:00 and some buses and the T4 tram diverted. At 14:00 Barça play Villarreal at the Spotify Camp Nou. In Montjuïc, Pavelló-Laberint, 343 glass panels set into the Barcelona Pavilion by Ciro Najle and Josep Ferrando, closes that day.
items.why: Taxi or tender to the city before eight, or go by metro; plan the Mies pavilion for the afternoon.
facts: Sun 22 Nov 2026: run 09:00; match 14:00; labyrinth until 22 Nov
Sant Martí and the Eixample; Les Corts; Montjuïc
Run free to watch; match and pavilion ticketed

groups.title: Christmas comes in
groups.desc: Lights on the 26th, a cathedral-front fair and a Christmas fair at the basilica, and a modernista hospital lit up.

items.name: The Christmas lights, Thursday 26 November
items.teaser: The lights go on at 18:00 on Passeig de Gràcia, and Plaça Sant Jaume becomes a moving Christmas card
items.story: On Thursday 26 November the city switches on nearly 140 km of Christmas lights with a show on Passeig de Gràcia, between Rosselló and Diagonal, at 18:00, and choirs in every district. The giant galet, Ramon Bigas's pasta-shell lamp, is back in twelve markets. In Plaça Sant Jaume the artist Alba G. Corral projects a growing winter landscape onto City Hall and the Generalitat from 26 November to 5 January, with a live opening on 27 November at 20:00.
items.why: Walk Passeig de Gràcia after dinner on a weekday; the Sant Jaume projections run sessions with music at 18:30, 19:30 and 20:30.
facts: Lights 26 Nov–6 Jan, 17:30–01:00 (to 02:00 Fri, Sat and holiday eves); Sant Jaume 26 Nov–5 Jan
Passeig de Gràcia; Plaça Sant Jaume
No Sant Jaume projections on 30 Nov or 1, 3 and 10 Dec; choir concerts there 12 Dec 19:00 and 19 Dec 20:00

items.name: The Christmas fairs: the basilica, then the Cathedral
items.teaser: 70-plus stalls at the Sagrada Família from 21 November, the Cathedral's fair from 27; both to 23 December
items.story: Two fairs mark the season. The Fira de Nadal de la Sagrada Família fills the square in front of the basilica from Saturday 21 November with more than 70 stalls: fir trees, nativity figures, turrón, honey and cheese, and churros, with a new children's space this year. The older fair, Santa Llúcia, in front of the Cathedral, opens on 27 November by the Generalitat's agenda; its story has its own card in the calendar. Both close on 23 December.
items.why: Do the basilica fair on a weekday morning, then come back for the Cathedral one after it opens.
facts: Sagrada Família 21 Nov–23 Dec 2026; Santa Llúcia 27 Nov–23 Dec 2026 (both 10:00–21:00)
Plaça de la Sagrada Família; Avinguda de la Catedral

items.name: Sant Pau after dark: the Little Prince in light
items.teaser: The modernista hospital pavilions become a light trail and an ice rink, 19 November to 10 January
items.story: Lluís Domènech i Montaner's Hospital de Sant Pau, the Art Nouveau complex at the far end of Avinguda de Gaudí, opens after dark this winter for Els Llums de Sant Pau: El Petit Príncep, a walk through projections and light and sound installations drawn from Saint-Exupéry's book, with live characters and an ice rink. It runs from 19 November 2026 to 10 January 2027. The point is less the show than seeing the tiled pavilions at night.
items.why: Pair it with the Sagrada Família fair: walk the ten minutes up Avinguda de Gaudí between them.

items.name: The MICHELIN Guide Spain 2027, now Tuesday 1 December
items.teaser: The gala moved a week because of the general election: the stars come out on 1 December, in Huesca
items.story: MICHELIN had set its Spain 2027 gala for 24 November in Huesca, the first ever in Aragón. When the general election was called for 29 November, the guide moved the night to Tuesday 1 December at 19:00, in the Auditorio Carlos Saura of the Palacio de Congresos, so it would not be lost in the vote count. Anne Igartiburu presents, and eight chefs from Huesca cook, led by Carmelo Bosque. For Barcelona, the night decides whether its star tables hold or move.
items.why: If a table on the guest list is likely to move up, book it before 1 December, not after.
facts: Palacio de Congresos de Huesca (Aragón), not Barcelona

items.name: The Barcelona Jazz Festival: the last five weeks
items.teaser: Vicente Amigo at the Palau on 20 November, Israel Fernández on the 27th, the closing night on 23 December
items.story: The 58th Voll-Damm Barcelona Jazz Festival runs into its final stretch. At the Palau de la Música: Vicente Amigo on Friday 20 November, the flamenco singer Israel Fernández on 27 November, Las Migas' carols on 3 December, Así Canta Jerez en Navidad on 12 December. The Sant Andreu Jazz Band closes the festival there on 23 December, marking its own 20 years. In between, the Jamboree on Plaça Reial runs two sets most nights, including the Eddie Henderson Quartet on 24–25 November.
items.why: Choose one Palau night for the modernista hall; take the Jamboree's early set for a club evening before dinner.
facts: To Wed 23 Dec 2026; Palau 20 Nov, 27 Nov, 3 Dec, 12 Dec, 23 Dec

items.name: La clemenza di Tito at the Liceu, conducted by Jordi Savall
items.teaser: Mozart's last opera, four nights from 25 November; The Nutcracker 8–12 December; La bohème from 30th
items.story: The Liceu's next staging is Mozart's last opera, La clemenza di Tito, in David McVicar's production from Aix-en-Provence, with Jordi Savall conducting his period orchestra Le Concert des Nations and Marianne Crebassa as Sesto. There are four performances only: 25, 27 and 29 November and 1 December. In December the house turns to ballet, with the Badisches Staatsballett Karlsruhe's Nutcracker from 8 to 12 December, then opens La bohème on 30 December.
items.why: Four nights only: book now, and take the upper tiers to see the horseshoe hall.
facts: Gran Teatre del Liceu, La Rambla
Ticketed; check liceubarcelona.cat (listings give €15 to about €400)

groups.title: The vote, the holidays, the sea and the sky
groups.desc: A general election on 29 November, the December holidays, cooler water and the year's best meteor shower.

items.name: Spain votes on Sunday 29 November
items.teaser: A snap general election: the campaign ends Friday 27, Saturday is the day of reflection, Sunday the vote
items.story: The government dissolved the Cortes on 6 October and called a general election for Sunday 29 November 2026 (Real Decreto 806/2026). The campaign runs to midnight on Friday 27 November; Saturday 28 is the legally silent day of reflection, and Sunday is polling day, with schools used as polling stations. The new Congress and Senate sit on 23 December. For a visitor it changes little, but expect rallies in the last week and the result to fill Sunday night.
items.why: Nothing closes for the vote, but book Sunday dinner: the city stays in to watch the count.
facts: Campaign to Fri 27 Nov; reflection Sat 28; vote Sun 29 Nov 2026
Avoid Plaça Sant Jaume and party venues on results night if you want a quiet evening

items.name: The December holidays, and Barça's home nights
items.teaser: Holidays on Tue 8, Fri 25 and Sat 26 December; Barça at home on 2, 5 and 8 December and 20 December
items.story: December has three holidays in Catalonia: Tuesday 8 December (the Immaculada), Christmas Day and Saint Stephen's Day on Saturday 26 December. The Constitution Day, 6 December, falls on a Sunday in 2026 and is not moved, so there is no long bridge. Markets and many shops close on holidays. Barça play at the Spotify Camp Nou on Wednesday 2 December against Atlético, Saturday 5 December against Celta, Tuesday 8 December against Manchester City in the Champions League, and on 20 December against Real Sociedad.
items.why: Shop on the 7th, not the 8th; on match nights, avoid Les Corts and the L3 and L5 metro after the final whistle.
facts: Holidays 8, 25, 26 Dec 2026; home matches 2 Dec 21:30, 5 Dec 21:00, 8 Dec 21:00, 20 Dec (time TBA)
Barcelona; Spotify Camp Nou, Les Corts

items.name: Cooler water, short days, and the Geminids under a dark sky
items.teaser: The sea at 18.5°C, sunset near 17:25, a full Moon on 24 November and the Geminids on 13–14 December
items.story: The sea read 18.5°C on 20 November, about a degree above normal, and keeps falling towards its February low near 13°C: wetsuit water now. Sunset is about 17:27 and comes earliest around 8 December; the solstice is on Monday 21 December at 21:50. The full Moon is on 24 November and the new Moon on 9 December, so the Geminids, the year's richest meteor shower, peak on the night of 13–14 December with only a thin crescent that sets early.
items.why: At anchor, the Geminids are best after midnight on the 13th; look high, away from the city glow.
facts: Full Moon Tue 24 Nov; new Moon 9 Dec; Geminids night of 13–14 Dec; solstice 21 Dec 2026
A 4/3 mm wetsuit is enough for a short swim now

groups.title: Spring: the book, the rose and the sound
groups.desc: Sant Jordi in April, then two festivals that fill June.

items.name: Sant Jordi, 23 April
items.teaser: Catalonia's day of the book and the rose: the whole city becomes a bookstall
items.story: On 23 April, the feast of Sant Jordi, Catalonia's patron saint, the custom is to give a rose and a book. The Rambla, Passeig de Gràcia and every square fill with bookstalls and rose sellers, authors sign at trestle tables, and it is a working day, so the crowd comes at lunch and after work. In 2027 it falls on a Friday.
items.why: Walk Passeig de Gràcia at midday and buy one book and one rose: that is the whole ritual.
facts: La Rambla, Passeig de Gràcia and squares citywide
Free to walk; books and roses for sale
It is a working day: the stalls are busiest at lunch and after 18:00

items.name: Primavera Sound, 2–6 June 2027
items.teaser: The big indie and pop festival at the Parc del Fòrum, with its 2027 line-up already out
items.story: Primavera Sound takes over the Parc del Fòrum, the concrete esplanade at the end of the Diagonal by the sea, for its early-June edition. The 2027 dates are 2–6 June, with the main programme on 3–5 June and opening and closing events around it; the line-up was announced in October 2026 and tickets went on sale on 8–9 October. Expect the Fòrum's stages to run from late afternoon until well after dawn.
items.why: Book hotels and berths early: the city is full for the festival weekend.
facts: The Fòrum is by the sea: a tender drop-off beats the metro crush

items.name: Sónar, mid-June
items.teaser: Barcelona's festival of advanced music and new media art: by day at Fira Montjuïc, by night at Fira Gran Via
items.story: Sónar, the electronic music and digital arts festival founded in 1994, runs over three days in mid-June, with daytime programmes and late-night stages. In 2026 it ran from 18 to 20 June. A listing site gives 17–19 June 2027, but the festival had not published its 2027 line-up or venues when we checked, so treat those dates as a placeholder until the official announcement.
items.why: Wait for sonar.es before booking around it.
facts: Fira Montjuïc (day) and Fira Gran Via (night) in past editions

groups.title: Summer: fire and the festes
groups.desc: Sant Joan's bonfires, a month of theatre at Montjuïc and Gràcia's decorated streets.

items.name: Sant Joan, the night of 23 June
items.teaser: The shortest night: bonfires, fireworks, coca de Sant Joan and cava on the beaches
items.story: The revetlla de Sant Joan, on the night of 23 June, is Catalonia's midsummer: fireworks from dusk until long after midnight, bonfires, the flame brought from Canigó, and the coca de Sant Joan, a flat sweet bread topped with candied fruit and pine nuts, eaten with cava. The beaches fill until dawn, and 24 June is a holiday. In 2027 the night falls on a Wednesday.
items.why: Watch from the water if you can: the beaches are packed and fireworks go off at street level all night.
facts: Night of 23 Jun every year (Wed 23 Jun 2027)
Buy the coca from a pastry shop that afternoon; they sell out

items.name: Grec Festival, July
items.teaser: Barcelona's summer festival of theatre, dance and music, centred on the open-air Teatre Grec on Montjuïc
items.story: The Grec began in 1976 and marked its 50th anniversary in 2026, running from 29 June to 31 July across some fifty spaces in the city. Its heart is the Teatre Grec, an open-air amphitheatre cut into a former quarry on Montjuïc in 1929, where the big productions play under the summer sky. 2027 dates are not yet published; it usually runs from the end of June through July.
items.why: Book a night at the Teatre Grec itself and arrive early to sit in the garden.
facts: Teatre Grec, Passeig de Santa Madrona 36, Montjuïc, and venues citywide
Bring a layer: Montjuïc evenings cool after dark

sources.label: CCCB: Grec 2026
This is Barcelona: main events (Grec 29 June–31 July 2026)

items.name: Festes de Gràcia, mid-August
items.teaser: A week when Gràcia's streets compete with hand-made decorations, with concerts every night
items.story: Each August the Gràcia district holds its festa major, and its streets and squares dress themselves in decorations that residents build over months, competing in the Concurs de Carrers Guarnits. In 2026 the festival ran 15–21 August, opened on 14 August, with 23 decorated streets and squares and more than 900 activities. It usually starts on 15 August, the feast of the Assumption, and the streets are judged early in the week.
items.why: Go in the morning to see the decorations without the night crowd.
facts: Usually 15 Aug for a week (2026: 15–21 Aug)
The decorations are best seen by day; the concerts run late

groups.title: Autumn and winter: the city's own
groups.desc: The national day, the patron's festival and the Christmas fair with its canelons.

items.name: La Diada, 11 September
items.teaser: Catalonia's national day: flags on the balconies, wreaths, and marches through the centre
items.story: The Diada Nacional de Catalunya on 11 September marks the fall of Barcelona in 1714 at the end of the siege in the War of the Spanish Succession. The day is a holiday, with flowers laid at the monument to Rafael Casanova, senyeres on the balconies and, in many years, large marches along the main avenues. Shops and many restaurants close for the day. In 2027 it falls on a Saturday.
items.why: Expect road closures in the centre: plan transfers around the march.
facts: Many shops close; book lunch ahead

items.name: La Mercè, around 24 September
items.teaser: Barcelona's own festival: giants, human towers, correfoc and free concerts
items.story: The city's festa major honours the Mare de Déu de la Mercè, patron of Barcelona, whose day, 24 September, is a local holiday. In 2026 the festival ran Wednesday 23 to Sunday 27 September, with Shanghai as guest city and events spread for the first time across all ten districts. Expect the gegants, castells in Plaça Sant Jaume, the correfoc and free concerts. In 2027 the 24th falls on a Friday.
items.why: See the castells in Plaça Sant Jaume on the morning of the 24th.
facts: Around 24 Sep (2026: 23–27 Sep; 24 Sep 2027 is a Friday)
Citywide; Plaça Sant Jaume for the castells
For the correfoc, cover arms and head with cotton

items.name: Fira de Santa Llúcia and Sant Esteve canelons
items.teaser: The Christmas fair in front of the Cathedral, then canelons on 26 December
items.story: The Fira de Santa Llúcia, the Christmas market on the Pla de la Seu and Avinguda de la Catedral, dates back to 1786 and sells nativity figures, moss, holly, caganers and the Tió de Nadal log. In 2026 the Generalitat's agenda gives 27 November to 23 December, 10:00 to 21:00, with more than 160 stalls. On Sant Esteve, 26 December, a holiday in Catalonia, families eat canelons made from the Christmas meat.
items.why: Buy a caganer at the fair; eat the canelons at a traditional house after Christmas.
facts: 27 Nov–23 Dec 2026, 10:00–21:00 (Generalitat agenda; some listings say 26 or 28 Nov); Sant Esteve Sat 26 Dec 2026
